Thanks Marissa - helpful summary. A few clarifying questions from our platform/security side before the deep-dive: 

1) Multi-tenant model: we need the ability to have customer-scoped credentials (i.e., a key per tenant) and be able to rotate those keys without redeploying clients. Does Redwood support per-tenant service accounts or only org-level API keys?
2) Key rotation: can Redwood trigger rotation via an API / CI workflow, or do we need to push rotated keys manually? Any automation for rolling short-lived tokens?
3) KMS/HSM: we plan to use AWS KMS + CloudHSM for key material. Can Redwood integrate so that private signing keys never leave our KMS?
4) OAuth/JWT: do you support an OIDC client-credentials flow issuing short-lived JWTs that are accepted by Redwood, or are API keys the only option?
5) Route scoping: can we limit keys so embeddings clients cannot call generation endpoints (and vice versa)?

We also have a security questionnaire we might send - I can attach it if helpful. Please have Aditya include sample code for issuing and rotating tokens (Node is preferred).

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>

Hi Kyle / Nisha - thanks, great questions. High-level answers + implementation notes below; happy to walk through live on Thu.

1) Per-tenant credentials
- Redwood supports both org-level API keys and tenant-scoped service accounts. For per-customer isolation we recommend issuing a service account per tenant scoped to specific roles. Service accounts map to an internal identity and can be bound to projects/environments.

2) Key rotation & automation
- We provide Key Management APIs to create/rotate API keys programmatically. Typical pattern: create a new key, update the client config (or issue short-lived tokens), then deprecate the old key. For short-lived tokens we recommend OIDC client-credentials + token exchange, which avoids long-lived secrets on clients.

3) KMS/HSM integration
- Redwood supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (CMK) and can integrate with CloudHSM for signing operations. We also offer Redwood-hosted key rotation if customers prefer Redwood-managed keys. If you want the private key material to stay in your KMS, we support remote signing (we send a signing challenge that your KMS signs).

4) OAuth/JWT support
- Yes - we support OIDC client_credentials and JWTs signed by your identity provider. Exchange flow: client -> IdP (client_credentials) -> get JWT -> call Redwood with Bearer token. Optionally, Redwood can mint short-lived tokens via an exchange endpoint if you prefer a single-use ephemeral key.

5) Route-scoped keys / policy enforcement
- You can set fine-grained policies on keys/service accounts (e.g., allowed routes: /v1/embeddings only, or model-specific access). Policies are enforced at the gateway and logged for audit.

Notes on embeddings / reranker telemetry
- Embeddings and reranker calls include token metadata in audit logs but we never store raw token material in logs. Be mindful that prompt material (if included client-side) can appear in usage logs; Redwood offers masking and redaction options for PII-sensitive workloads.

References and snippets
- Auth docs: https://docs.redwood.inference/api/auth
- Quickstart (Node): https://docs.redwood.inference/quickstart/node#service-accounts
- Sample: auth-patterns-quickstart.md (attached)

If helpful, I can paste a short Node snippet on the call to show the client_credentials flow and token-exchange. Do you prefer Thu 3/4 11:00 PT for the technical deep-dive?

— Aditya

Thanks Aditya - that covers most of it. Couple follow-ups ahead of the deep-dive so we can make the meeting productive:

- Function-calling / structured output: we plan to use Redwood "tool calling" to invoke backend systems (e.g., payments, account provisioning). Are those outbound calls audited and tied to the originating API key/service-account? We need traceability for every external call initiated by the model.
- Token leakage concerns: if we pass any customer secrets in prompt context for retrieval-augmented generation, how do you recommend preventing those from appearing in logs or model cache?
- Per-route quotas & rate limiting: can quotas be applied per key and per model (embedding vs generation)? We need to enforce different SLAs for embeddings-heavy traffic vs interactive generation.

Also: please share an initial SOW/price expectation (we saw the draft attached to Marissa's email). We'll share the security questionnaire this afternoon.

— Kyle

Kyle / Nisha - quick confirmations ahead of the call and next artifacts we'll send: 

1) Outbound tool-calling auditability: yes - all function/tool invocations are logged and correlated to the originating request id and service-account. Logs include timestamp, initiating key id, target endpoint, and response metadata (no payload unless you opt in). We can include this in the security appendix.

2) Prompt/data leakage safeguards: Redwood provides prompt masking, redaction, and optional in-memory-only execution modes. For RAG scenarios we recommend passing retrieved documents via a transient vector store and using request-scoped encryption keys; we can walk through the pattern on Thu.

3) Quotas & rate limits: quotas can be applied per-service-account and per-route/model. We support tiered quotas (e.g., high-throughput embeddings pool vs low-latency generation pool) and can map these to Dedicated capacity if desired.

Next steps:
- We'll send the security appendix and SOC2 artifacts by EOD today.
- Updated SOW with a couple of pricing options will be shared by Mon 3/8.
- Confirming technical deep-dive: Thu 2026-03-04 11:00 PT - please confirm attendees and whether you want a calendar invite.
